import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ascending descending base exponent transform of factorials

*References:*
- [A113258](https://oeis.org/A113258)
-/

namespace OeisA113258

open Nat

/--
The primary defining sequence `a`.
$a(n)$ is the ascending descending base exponent transform of factorials.
$$a(n) = \sum_{i = 1}^n (i!) ^ {(n-i+1)!}$$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, (i + 1)! ^ (n - i)!

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 3 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 11 := by rfl

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 125 := by rfl

/--
Is there a nontrivial power after $a(4) = 5^3$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture :
  answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ n > 4, ∃ b > 1, ∃ e > 1, a n = b ^ e := by
  sorry

end OeisA113258

reformulations.difference: Lean sums over i = 0,…,n−1 with summand ((i+1)!)^((n−i)!), whereas OEIS sums over j = 1,…,n with summand (j!)^((n−j+1)!).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The substitution j = i+1 is a bijection between these index sets. Since i < n, natural-number subtraction satisfies n−(i+1)+1 = n−i. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, proved equality with the OEIS formula for every n and the induced equivalence of the complete perfect-power existence statements. The extension a(0)=0 is harmless because the question requires n>4.

sources_consulted: OEIS A113258, complete entry (revision #13, June 8, 2025), read through the OEIS data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A113/A113258.seq
review.notes: Checked all six declarations. The four test values agree with OEIS, and the conjecture faithfully asks its question: “Is there a nontrivial power after a(4) = 5^3?” All three existential variables are natural numbers; the bounds and answer scope are correct. Lean computations matched every b-file term, verified a(4)=5^3, and found no perfect-power witness at the first permitted index n=5. The consulted entry records no resolution, consistent with research open. The main OEIS page was browser-challenge blocked, so its complete text was read through the OEIS data mirror; the b-file was accessible directly. The final scratch file compiled without errors and its equivalence proofs do not depend on sorryAx.
